title: Why Do Safety Guardrails Degrade Across Languages?

bias_targets.methodology: Applying a Multi-Group Item Response Theory (IRT) framework to decouple a model's intrinsic safety robustness from language-specific processing difficulty and prompt-specific cross-lingual safety gaps (Differential Item Functioning).

Using native speaker annotations to evaluate prompts that exhibit high cross-lingual safety gaps despite perfect translation quality, identifying culturally foreign concepts and cultural framing shifts.
Comparing LLM-as-a-judge safety evaluations against human native speaker ratings and cross-judge agreements to test for English-centric bias, translation noise artifacts, and model family self-bias.
